ADR text (for DECISIONS.md): "ADR: APP_SECRET rotation with one previous key. Ciphertexts carry the id (sha256 of the secret, first 8 hex) of the key that sealed them (v2); v1 ciphertexts are opened with every configured key. APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS holds the old key during a rotation and scripts/rotate-secret.ts re-encrypts every stored secret with the current key; no KMS. Domain-proof TXT values derive from APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET (default APP_SECRET), documented as set once and never rotated; during a rotation either key's record is accepted. Signed values are not re-signed. One verified domain per organisation is enforced by the partial unique index tenants_domain_verified_idx; the actions answer domainTaken."
PROGRESS line: "B2-secrets: S-07 closed (key ids, APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS, rotate script, runbook), S-11 (b) closed (tenants_domain_verified_idx, domainTaken in ten locales)."

## reviews
approve
Reviewed worktree wf_42496c94-3d0-2 at d4099f1 (two commits: aa24f2c and a follow-up d4099f1 that adds rotationRefusal, withDefaults in the rotation, a conditional TOTP update and an audit entry on the operator's refused proof). Base contains 1a45970; nothing under portal/drizzle or docs/build is committed (0004 migration and journal change are uncommitted, as required). Ran in the worktree: `npm run typecheck` (pass), `npx eslint src tests scripts --max-warnings=0` (pass), `npx vitest run tests/crypto.test.ts tests/auth.test.ts tests/settings-rate-limit.test.ts tests/auth-security.test.ts` (4 files, 96 tests pass).

Attacker lens, what held: (1) a forged or unknown kid in a v2 ciphertext only widens the key search; the GCM tag rejects every wrong key, and the v1 parse path is byte-identical (pinned by V1_FIXTURE). (2) A leaked previous key gives nothing new during the rotation window: signValue/unsignValue (SSO state) use the current key only, so old-key SSO state cannot be forged; domain-proof values derived from the previous key still require control of the domain's DNS; backup-code hashes under the previous key need database write access to plant. (3) The verified-domain index cannot be bypassed by case, trailing dot or Unicode variants (normaliseHost lower-cases and IDNA-converts before the lookup and the write); two organisations racing on one domain are serialised by the index and the loser gets domainTaken with its row unchanged (tested); an organisation's own re-check and an unverified duplicate are allowed by design; sign-in routing (actions/auth.ts:217), people.ts:88 and jobs.ts:302 all filter on domain_verified_at, so an unverified duplicate row gains nothing. (4) The domainTaken answer in verifyDomainAction is only reachable when the caller's own proof record resolves on that domain (found), so it leaks 'another organisation verified this' only to someone who controls the DNS anyway. (5) The rotate script locks each tenant row, updates users.totp_secret conditionally on the ciphertext it read, skips values already under the current key (idempotent, tested), never destroys an unreadable value, and refuses the development key whenever DATABASE_URL or NODE_ENV=production is set. (6) Every encryptSecret consumer in src (sso.clientSecretEnc, ldap.passwordEnc, email.passwordEnc, integrations.webhookSecretEnc, users.totp_secret) is covered by the rotation; no other encrypted field exists in schema.ts. (7) withDefaults spreads the raw settings, so the write-back drops no unknown keys. (8) Ten locales carry both domainTaken keys, no 'Aİ', no ICU braces; toasts use the namespaces the components already hold (settings.branding, admin.platform).

Nothing of severity blocker or major remains; the minor items are operational guards and docs the orchestrator or a follow-up can take. Not checked: a rotation against a real PostgreSQL (tests use PGlite; the pg driver's unique-violation error carries `constraint`, which db/errors.ts handles the same way); the standalone image was not built.

Not exploitable (the AES key is sha256('enc:'+secret), GCM tags already allow offline key guessing), but purpose-tagged derivation is the conventional hygiene; changing it later would change the id of every v2 value (the fallback still opens them). -> Optional: `createHash("sha256").update(`kid:${value}`)`; if changed, do it now before v2 values exist in production.

approve
I approve this package. No blocker or major findings remain.

What I checked:
- Worktree contents: it contains 1a45970. There are two commits: aa24f2c, plus d4099f1, which adds the rotationRefusal guard, a conditional TOTP reseal and an audit when the operator's domain proof is refused. The local 0004 migration and the journal change are untracked; nothing under portal/drizzle is committed. The generated SQL is a correct partial unique index.
- Checks I ran myself, all passing:
  - `npm run typecheck`
  - `npx eslint src tests scripts --max-warnings=0`
  - vitest on tests/crypto, auth, settings-rate-limit, password-domain, tenant-settings, jobs-ops, jobs-runner, drill-service, syslog, auth-actions-session, auth-security, secops-flows, sso-routes and rtl-logical (14 files).
- v1 compatibility: the key derivation sha256("enc:"+secret) is unchanged, and the v1 split and parse behave as before. The fixture decrypts under the current key and also under the previous key. v2 routes by key id, and an unknown key id falls back to every key.
- Coverage of stored secrets: the only places encryptSecret is called are the four tenants.settings *Enc fields and users.totp_secret, and the rotation covers exactly that set. The rotation is idempotent: values already sealed with the current key are skipped, and unreadable values are counted. Each tenant row is locked, and the TOTP update is conditional.
- Domain proof: every check site (settings, platform, jobs) uses domainProofRecords. The published record comes from env.domainProofSecret, and the pre-change derivation is pinned by a fixture.
- Backup codes: the `codes.map(c => hashBackupCode(c))` fix is needed, because a bare `.map(hashBackupCode)` would pass the array index as the secret.
- Domain uniqueness: both writers catch isUniqueViolation('tenants_domain_verified_idx'), return domainTaken and audit it. The client toasts use the right namespaces (settings.branding and admin.platform). The keys are present in all ten locales, with no ICU braces and no "Aİ" in Azerbaijani. Only the demo organisation in the seed has a verified domain.
- Docs: the runbook and the README/.env.example entries match decisions (f) and (h).

Accepted residual risks (the owner's open questions 1-3): pre-rotation backup codes stop working at step 4; APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET must be set before the first rotation; and the migration needs no existing duplicate verified domains.

Not checked: the full test suite (the orchestrator runs it), and running scripts/rotate-secret.ts end to end against a real database.
- [minor] portal/tests/crypto.test.ts:176 The acceptance item says backup codes keep working during a rotation, but the test only checks that backupCodeHashes() lists the previous-key hash. Nothing runs spendBackupCode or verifySecondFactorAction against a stored code that was hashed with APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS, so a regression in the auth.ts loop or in the SQL `totpRecovery - h` update would not be caught. -> Add one case: give a user totpRecovery [hashBackupCode(code, PREVIOUS)], turn rotation on, and check the second-factor path accepts the code once and removes it. Then turn rotation off and check a second such code is refused.
- [minor] docs/OPERATIONS.md:128 Step 3 says to run `npx tsx scripts/rotate-secret.ts` from the portal folder. The runtime image ships neither tsx nor scripts/*.ts (Dockerfile lines 35-44). A compose deployment therefore has no documented way to run the step, even though the compose `seed` service already shows the pattern: builder stage plus `npx tsx`. The implementer raised this as open question 4. -> Add the compose command to step 3, e.g. `docker compose --profile tools run --rm --entrypoint npx seed tsx scripts/rotate-secret.ts`, with APP_SECRET/APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS/DATABASE_URL passed in. Alternatively, record it for the owner as a follow-up.
- [nit] portal/src/server/services/secret-rotation.ts:44 If a tenant is deleted after the id list is read and before its row is locked, `row` is undefined and `row.settings` throws, which aborts the whole run. Rerunning recovers, because the run is idempotent. -> `if (!row) return false;` after the locked select.
- [nit] portal/src/server/env.ts:22 env.test.ts has no case for APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS or APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET: the under-32 rejection and the domainProofSecret fallback chain (APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET, then APP_SECRET, then the dev secret) are untested. The implementer noted this. -> Add one env.test.ts case covering the short-value rejection and the fallback order.

Finding 4 (crypto.test.ts backup codes): portal/tests/auth-security.test.ts gets a case that stores two codes hashed with APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS, runs verifySecondFactorAction with rotation on (first code accepted once, second attempt refused), then with rotation off (the other code refused and still stored). The env mock there became a hoisted object so previousSecret can be toggled.
rejected:
Finding 3 (partial unique index tenants_domain_verified_idx failing on existing duplicate verified domains): not a code change for this package; it is an owner/orchestrator step at wave-migration time. Left open for the owner: run `select domain, count(*) from tenants where domain_verified_at is not null group by domain having count(*) > 1` before the wave migration; if rows come back, the orchestrator prefixes the generated migration with an UPDATE that nulls domain_verified_at on all but the oldest row per domain (the seed only verifies the demo organisation, so local and compose seeds are unaffected).
